note: Every tab plate in the game: the word painted on it, UNLIT (slate navy, steel rim) and LIT (crimson, gold rim), from art/reference/tabs_sheet_a.png (355x88 crops), tabs_sheet_b.png (389x87) and tabs_sheet_c.png (254x80: the short plates, tabs/short_<word>, about three to one, for the strips of three and four -- the long plates drawn four abreast shrank to 0.54 and their words went thinner than the painting's). Each crop is one size for its sheet and centred on its own plate's ink -- the plate's outline, found by flooding the ground in from the crop's border -- so a plate and its word stay put when a tab lights (the short plates across between their plate's ink and their word's, whose painter set a lit word a pixel or two off its unlit twin, and down on the plate's own foot, two above the crop's, so every short plate stands on its strip's floor); the polygon is that outline, so the plate sits on any ground. Kept at the painting's size and drawn down by scripts/ui/tab_strip.gd, which never stretches one.
